               <ns0:p n="42">42 And when they had nothing to pay, he frankly forgave them both. Tell me therefore, Which of them will love him most.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="43">43 Simon answered and said, I suppose that he to whom he forgave most. And he said unto him, Thou hast rightly judged.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="44">44 And he turned to the woman, and said unto Simon, Seest thou this woman? I entred into thine house, thou gavest me no water for my feet, but she hath washed my feet with tears, and wiped <ns0:hi>them</ns0:hi> with the hairs of her head.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="45">45 Thou gavest me no kiss: but this woman, since the time I came in, hath not ceased to kiss my feet.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="46">46 Mine head with oil thou didst not anoint, but this woman hath anointed my feet with oint<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="47">47 Wherefore I say unto thee, Her sins, which are many, are forgiven; for she loved much: but to whom little is forgiven, the same loveth little.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="48">48 And he said unto her, Thy sins are forgiven.<ns0:note place="bottom">Our Saviour treateth his host civilly, but yet letteth him know, that he both knew his heart, and the heart of this poor Woman, whom he had so uncharitably reflected upon. <ns0:hi>Simon v.</ns0:hi> 39. <ns0:hi>spake within himself.</ns0:hi> Christ lets him know that he knew the thoughts of his heart. <ns0:hi>I have,</ns0:hi> (saith he) <ns0:hi>something to say unto thee.</ns0:hi> So he civilly obtaineth leave of him to speake, <ns0:hi>Simon</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Master say on.</ns0:hi> Our Saviour tells him. <ns0:hi>There was a cer<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tain Creditor,</ns0:hi> &c. It is obvious by our Saviours application of this Parable <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 44, 45, 46, 47. That he whom Christ here in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tendeth under the notion of a <ns0:hi>Creditor</ns0:hi> is God. That one of the debtors that did owe five hundred pence, (that is a great Sum,) was this <ns0:hi>Woman,</ns0:hi> whither <ns0:hi>Simon</ns0:hi> were intended by the other or no, is not easily determined, but admit the other was <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> any one that was a Sinner, but not so notorious a Sinner. God for<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gives freely both the one and the other. Christ asks which would love most? <ns0:hi>Simon</ns0:hi> tells him, that Debtor to whom most was forgiven. Christ tells him that he had judged rightly, whence observe. 1. That as all Sins, so all Sinness are not equal in the sight of God, all are guilty, but there are degrees in guilt. 2. That be Mens Sins less or greater, fewer, or more, those who have least will stand in need of pardoning Mercy, and forgivness. 3. That God is free in the forgivness of all Sins, be they few or more. <ns0:hi>He frankly forgave them both.</ns0:hi> 4. That Christ first speaketh of these two <ns0:hi>Debtors</ns0:hi> as being <ns0:hi>forgiven</ns0:hi> them, of their <ns0:hi>loving much</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and of their being <ns0:hi>forgiven</ns0:hi> as the cause of their loving much 5. That much love, will follow a great forgivness, a great Sinner (one I mean who hath been so) will hardly ever be able to satisfie himself, that his much is forgiven, if he doth not find his heart very warm with Love to God. 6. A true Love to God and Christ, will be seen in all acts, which may be demonstrative or declarative of it. Christ turns to the Woman, and saith to <ns0:hi>Simon,</ns0:hi> &c. <ns0:hi>Kissing, washing of feet, anointing with Oil,</ns0:hi> were usual Com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />plements of those Countries, by which Men shewed their respects and kindness to <ns0:hi>Strangers</ns0:hi> and Friends. For <ns0:hi>Washing</ns0:hi> of Feet. See <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 18.4 <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 19 2. <ns0:hi>Iud.</ns0:hi> 29 21. 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 25.41. 1 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 5.10. <ns0:hi>For anointing with Oil.</ns0:hi> See <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 23.5 <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 45.7. This Woman had exceeded the usual kindness, and civility of the Country to<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ward Christ, they were wont to bring their Friends Water to wash their Feet, and possibly a piece of linnen to wipe them, she washeth his Feet with her tears, and drieth them with her hair. They used to annoint the <ns0:hi>Head</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>of their Friends with <ns0:hi>Oil,</ns0:hi> she annoints his <ns0:hi>Feet.</ns0:hi> They used to kiss one anothers <ns0:hi>Cheeks</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> or <ns0:hi>Lips,</ns0:hi> she kisseth his Feet, they kissed their Friends <ns0:hi>once,</ns0:hi> she ceased not to kiss his Feet. Upon this Christ who before had forgiven her, <ns0:hi>declareth</ns0:hi> her to be forgiven, first in the hearing of <ns0:hi>Simon,</ns0:hi> then he doubleth his Words unto her. He had told <ns0:hi>Simon</ns0:hi> before that the Creditor had <ns0:hi>frankly forgiven them both,</ns0:hi> his adding here, <ns0:hi>Her sins which are many,</ns0:hi> sufficiently evidenceth that she was she, whom he intended by the debtor <ns0:hi>who owed much.</ns0:hi> Hence we may judge how little ground the <ns0:hi>Papists</ns0:hi> have, to urge this place to prove, <ns0:hi>that Remission of Sins is procured by our own merits and satisfactions.</ns0:hi> Love here is not mentioned as the cause, but as the effect of the Remission of Sins, and that which our Saviour here designed to in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />struct <ns0:hi>Simon</ns0:hi> in, was. 1. That whatsoever this Woman had been, she was not now such a notorious Sinner, as he fancyed; her Sins were forgiven. 2. That God having thus favoured her with the Grace of Remission, had also kindled in her heart a Love towards him. 3. That this Love wrought in her heart in some proportion to that Love, which God had magnified upon her, therefore she loved much. 4. That Men and Womens love to God and Christ, will, and ought to be according to that Love which they have re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceived from Christ. 5. That much love to God, will bring a great sense of Gods Love to the Soul. <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 14.21. The Particle <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> which we Translate <ns0:hi>because,</ns0:hi> doth not always in Scripture signifie the cause, but may be translate <ns0:hi>therefore,</ns0:hi> or for <ns0:hi>what cause,</ns0:hi> see <ns0:hi>Ioh</ns0:hi> 14.17. <ns0:hi>you know him for he dwelleth in you,</ns0:hi> the Spirits a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />biding in believers, is not the cause of their knowing of him<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> but the effect of it, so that <ns0:hi>for,</ns0:hi> in that place is as much as <ns0:hi>therefore,</ns0:hi> So in <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> 9.28. <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> is as much as <ns0:hi>for what cause,</ns0:hi> or, <ns0:hi>for what reason</ns0:hi>? we translate it, <ns0:hi>why</ns0:hi> could not we cast him out, so here, <ns0:hi>Her Sins which are many are forgiven,</ns0:hi> for which cause, or reason, she loveth much.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="49">49 And they that sat at meat with him, began to say within themselves, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Matth. 9.3.</ns0:note> Who is this that forgiveth sins also?<ns0:note place="bottom">These were either the <ns0:hi>Pharisees,</ns0:hi> who thought that Christ blasphemed, in arogating to himself such a Power as belonged to God alone, or the others, who speak this rather in admiration, but it is probable the former are here meant.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="50">50 And he said to the woman, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mark 10.52. Chap. 8.48 <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 18.42.</ns0:note> Thy faith hath saved thee; go in peace.<ns0:note place="bottom">Thy believing in me as <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>e who have Power on Earth to forgive Sins, and accordingly making application to me, and this thy Faith <ns0:hi>working by Love, Gal.</ns0:hi> 5.6. producing in thee this hearty sorrow for thy Sins, a subjection unto me, and such testifications of thy Love as thou art able to make, hath been an instru<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mental cause of that Salvation, which floweth from me as the principal cause. <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 6.23. we have such another expression in <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 9.22. <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> 5.34. tho the <ns0:hi>saving</ns0:hi> here mentioned, be much more excellent then that there spoken of, Faith is profitable both for the good things of this Life, and those of the Life which is to come. And with reference to both, <ns0:hi>Salvation</ns0:hi> is ascribed to <ns0:hi>Faith,</ns0:hi> as the instrumental cause, not to <ns0:hi>Obedience</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Love,</ns0:hi> tho the Faith that doth us good must <ns0:hi>work by Love,</ns0:hi> and be evidenced by an <ns0:hi>Holy Conversation. Go in Peace,</ns0:hi> is a Phrase which was the usual valediction among the Jews, as much as our <ns0:hi>Farewell,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>God be with you,</ns0:hi> they under the term of <ns0:hi>Peace,</ns0:hi> comprehending all good, but when we consider who it is that speaketh, and what immediately preceeded, we have reason to think this was a more then ordinary <ns0:hi>Complement</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Farewell,</ns0:hi> even as much as is com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />prehended under the term <ns0:hi>Peace,</ns0:hi> which as I before said is <ns0:hi>all good,</ns0:hi> but more especially that <ns0:hi>Peace</ns0:hi> mentioned by the Apostle, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 5.1. as an effect of <ns0:hi>Faith.</ns0:hi> Go thy way a blessed, and happy Woman, and in the view and sence of they own blessedness, and be not troubled at the Censures and reflexions of supercilious Persons, who may despise or overlook thee because thou hast been a great Sinner. God hath pardoned thy Sins, and this I assure thee of, only take heed to keep and maintain that Peace.</ns0:note>
